items.title: Two 22-year-old women die in car fire after collision with lorry in Yong Peng
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 10 — Two 22-year-old women were burnt to death when their car caught fire following a collision with a lorry at Batu 1, Jalan Yong Peng-Ayer Hitam, yesterday afternoon. Ayer Hitam Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohd Shamin Mohamed Salikin said they received an emergency call at 4.21pm, and a team arrived at the scene four minutes later. Mohd Shamin said both victims were found burnt beyond recognition.

items.title: anak krakatau shows renewed activity, alert raised to level III
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano has shown renewed activity, recording at least 13 eruptions on Friday and prompting authorities to raise its alert status to Level III, the second-highest level in the country's four-tier volcanic alert system. The Geological Agency said the alert was raised from Level II effective 9 pm local time on Friday, following an assessment of volcanic activity since early this month. Anak Krakatau, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, was downgraded to Level II on Sept 21 following a reduction in volcanic activity, after remaining at Level III since early September.

items.title: RM12.47mil in cryptocurrency stolen from man's digital wallet
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the victim discovered the loss while he was in Teluk Intan about 1pm yesterday. He said preliminary investigations found that the transactions involved the transfer of cryptocurrency assets through a blockchain network. Alwi advised the public, particularly cryptocurrency and digital wallet users, to remain vigilant against phishing attempts and online scams.

items.title: SME association says Budget 2027 offers support, but warns of ‘cumulative’ cost pressures
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Association of Malaysia has welcomed the government’s Budget 2027 initiatives aimed at bolstering domestic consumption and promoting investment but cautioned that the cumulative cost of doing business remains the sector's most significant hurdle. The association's president Chin Chee Seong said that while the Budget introduces various measures to support businesses, the government must ensure these initiatives deliver measurable improvements to SME cash flow, productivity and competitiveness. We are asking for policies that deliver real and measurable results,” Chin told Malay Mail following the Budget announcement yesterday.

items.title: Malaysians welcome Budget aid, but seek long-term solutions to rising living costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians have welcomed measures in the 2027 Budget to ease financial pressures but called for longer-term solutions to rising living costs, employment challenges and education needs. Full-time GrabFood rider Ahyar Amat, 35, said the measures would help ease the burden of rising living costs, particularly for private-sector employees and gig workers. I think the measures are encouraging for Malaysians," he said.

items.title: Brazil police rescue 13 children held hostage, assailant dead
items.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO: Police in Brazil on Friday rescued 13 children who had been taken hostage at their kindergarten and killed the assailant who threatened to set fire to the building, officials said. At least one of the children was wounded, he added. The children became agitated and the attacker started hitting them, Lopes Dias told reporters.

items.title: India deploys police, restricts transport ahead of major protests
items.summary: New Delhi, Oct 10, 2026 (AFP) - India deployed thousands of police in its capital and restricted transportation in and around Delhi ahead of mass demonstrations on Saturday demanding the resignation of the country's election chief over alleged voter-roll irregularities. The protests, called by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), are the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision. Demonstrations erupted across the country after a newspaper investigation last month alleged misconduct by the Election Commission of India (ECI).

items.title: US says Chinese actions off Taiwan are 'deeply destabilising'
items.summary: TAIPEI: China's maritime actions off Taiwan's east coast are "deeply destabilising" and only worsen tensions, the US State Department said, after Reuters reported the first known sighting of a Chinese militia boat in those waters in August. China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island's east coast since June, with regular coast guard patrols. "China's actions are deeply destabilising," the spokesperson added.

items.title: Zara Qairina’s mum disputes diary entries expressing ‘hate’ towards her, says handwriting not daughter’s
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 10 — The mother of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir yesterday disputed the authenticity of several diary entries expressing hatred towards her, telling the Coroner's Court she had never seen her daughter write such things. Noraidah Lamat, 46, said she disagreed that the entries must have been Zara Qairina's, since anyone could have written them. “I disagree because I have never seen Zara Qairina's writing like this,” she said before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan yesterday in the inquest into the teenager's death.

items.title: Fourteen remanded as police probe death of 18-year-old found by Gurun roadside
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 10 — Fourteen people aged between 16 and 24 have been remanded to assist investigations into the death of an 18-year-old man whose body was found by the roadside in Gurun on Thursday. Bernama reported Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan as saying that 12 of the suspects were remanded for six days, while two minors were remanded for five days. The remand orders were issued by Magistrate Noor Fazlina Musa at the Sungai Petani Magistrates’ Court yesterday.

items.title: Man with 10 previous criminal offences shot after police chase
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A man with 10 previous criminal offences was shot and injured after leading police on a chase from Petaling Jaya towards Sungai Buloh while driving dangerously and ramming other vehicles yesterday. Petaling Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said the man, who is in his 30s, was driving a Proton Wira when police apprehended him. He said police received a report on the incident around 6.42pm.

items.title: Budget 2027: Grab aims to raise gig workers’ earnings without increasing fares
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Grab aims to increase the earnings of e-hailing drivers and p-hailing delivery partners from 2027 without affecting passenger fares under a proposed minimum earnings framework. In a statement yesterday, Grab said an agreement in principle had been reached on a proposed minimum baseline rate for e-hailing and p-hailing workers. The company also said its most active drivers and delivery partners would receive 100 per cent coverage for mandatory Social Security Organisation (SOCSO) contributions, while other partners would receive contribution subsidies of up to 50 per cent.

items.title: Lorry driver who rammed into 11 vehicles tests positive for drugs
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A lorry driver who rammed into 11 vehicles at a traffic light junction in Alam Budiman, Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, yesterday tested positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine. The collision , involving a 10-tonne lorry and 11 other vehicles at the traffic lights on Jalan Mokhtar Dahari, Section U10, left four people injured, including a 58-year-old man who sustained critical head injuries. Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said the 4.20pm collision involved 12 vehicles, including the 10-tonne lorry.

items.title: Malaysia, Egypt to hold bilateral talks today as El-Sisi makes first state visit
items.summary: “Welcome to Malaysia, President El-Sisi!” Malaysia and Egypt established diplomatic relations in 1959. Bilateral trade amounted to RM3.08 billion (US$0.72 billion), with Malaysian exports to Egypt valued at RM2.55 billion (US$0.60 billion) and imports from Egypt totalling RM530 million (US$120 million).

items.title: Having a baby? Budget 2027 proposes up to RM3,000 tax relief for postnatal care
items.summary: In its proposed Budget 2027 tabled in Parliament yesterday, the Finance Ministry also proposed to reclassify or rename the income tax relief of medical treatment into "Health and Well-being", and to keep the existing maximum tax relief for this category at RM10,000. Under this proposed renamed tax relief category of "Health and Well-being", the ministry proposed to expand it to cover these two expenses, starting from the tax assessment year of 2027: Tax relief for a maximum RM3,000 in "postnatal care service expenses provided by a confinement centre aor qualified individual"; Tax relief for a maximum RM1,000 for breastfeeding equipment for children aged two and below "paid by self or spouse". Recommended reading: Budget 2027: Individual tax relief rises to RM12,000, income tax percentage lowered

items.title: E-hailing, p-hailing workers welcome insurance cost relief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The RM160 million support package for e-hailing and p-hailing workers announced under the 2027 Budget, particularly vehicle insurance assistance, can ease operating costs and boost net income for drivers and riders facing rising premium rates. Persatuan Rakan Grab Malaysia (PRGM), representing over 20,000 members nationwide, said in a statement that rising insurance premiums were among the earliest issues raised during engagement sessions with Grab Malaysia since its establishment last month. PRGM acknowledged Grab Malaysia's initiative to offer daily insurance payment options to ease drivers' financial pressure, but noted that this focused primarily on payment flexibility and did not fully address overall premium hikes.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh seeks lasting solution to homelessness in Kuala Lumpur
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has been directed to review data on homeless people in the city centre collected through enforcement operations over the past three years. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the review was aimed at identifying the best solutions to address homelessness in the city centre. "I do not want us to simply keep repeating enforcement operations against homeless people.

items.title: #NSTviral: Boy waves, train honks, hearts melt in Kempas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A simple wave from a boy to a passing Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) train in Kempas, Johor, warmed hearts online after the driver returned the greeting with a wave and a honk. The moment, captured on video and shared on Threads by the boy's mother, user @_zrily, showed her son waving at the passing train before the driver responded. Delighted by the gesture, she took to social media to thank the driver for making her son's day.

items.title: Batu Pahat tops API readings at 190, 32 locations unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Batu Pahat recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 190 as of 8am today, as worsening haze affected several areas in Johor and Negri Sembilan. As of 8am, 32 locations nationwide recorded unhealthy API readings, while 36 showed moderate air quality. No locations recorded good or hazardous air quality.

items.title: 'Loe appeared in my dreams three times; he wants to come home'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nearly two months after losing contact with her husband following the floods disaster in Nepal, Hani Othman remains hopeful that Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa will return to his family. In a Facebook post today, Hani shared that her husband, better known as Loe, had appeared in her dreams three times, expressing his wish to return home. He wants to return," she said.

items.title: Chief Judge heads Sarawak Governor's birthday honours list
items.summary: She was conferred the Darjah Panglima Negara Bintang Sarawak (PNBS), which carries the title Datuk Seri. Meanwhile, four recipients were conferred the Darjah Panglima Gemilang Bintang Kenyalang (PGBK), which carries the title Datuk. A total of 71 individuals received the Ahli Bintang Sarawak, 241 were conferred the Ahli Bintang Kenyalang, 365 the Pingat Perkhidmatan Terpuji, while 284 received the Bentara Bintang Sarawak.

items.title: 2027 Budget: "Balance, discipline and pragmatic" [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget strikes a pragmatic balance between fiscal consolidation, economic growth and cost-of-living support, economists say. However, its success will depend on whether public spending translates into higher household incomes, better jobs and stronger productivity. Universiti Teknologi Mara senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said the budget struck a reasonable balance between supporting economic growth, easing cost-of-living pressures and managing public finances.

items.title: Saudi-led coalition says destroyed more than 100 Houthi targets
items.summary: RIYADH (Saudi Arabia): The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said today it destroyed more than 100 military targets in a "large-scale operation" against the Iran-backed group. "We destroyed 136 military targets in areas controlled by the Houthi terrorist militia," he said in a separate post. The Houthi's Almasirah TV channel reported that Saudi missiles targeted areas in the northwestern Yemeni governorate of Saada.

items.title: Trump appoints 'devoted fan' Katie Zacharia as press secretary
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Friday announced the appointment of conservative commentator Katie Zacharia as his new White House press secretary, praising her as a loyal supporter. Trump praised his new spokeswoman's credentials, including her work for his presidential campaigns, and said he was confident she would enjoy a good relationship with the White House press corps. Zacharia thanked Trump in a post on X for the "distinguished privilege of serving as White House Press Secretary".

items.title: Protests in New York as Trump administration defends ICE shooting
items.summary: NEW YORK: Protesters gathered in New York on Friday after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers shot a Dominican man in an incident that has provoked a showdown between the city's Democratic mayor and the Trump administration. The shooting drew swift criticism from Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who wrote "Abolish ICE" on X — a common refrain among the political left opposed to Republican President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown. Mullin said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Brazil prosecutors sue Shell for US$108mil over deadly 2024 floods
items.summary: BRASILIA: Brazilian prosecutors on Friday filed an unprecedented lawsuit against oil giant Shell's subsidiary in the country, demanding US$108 million in compensation over deadly 2024 floods. According to the lawsuit, Shell's liability should match its contribution to global warming, estimated at two per cent of historical global greenhouse gas emissions. The filing of a new climate-related lawsuit by Brazilian prosecutors, in conjunction with Instituto Preservar, a Brazilian NGO, marks a new phase in the global legal battle against oil giants.

items.title: Trump takes suit against Hillary Clinton over 2016 election to Supreme Court
items.summary: NEW YORK: President Donald Trump asked the US Supreme Court on Friday to revive his dismissed lawsuit against his 2016 Democratic rival Hillary Clinton, accusing her, former FBI Director James Comey and others of conspiring to rig that year's election by linking his campaign to Russia. In 2022, after losing the 2020 election and leaving office, Trump sued Clinton, Comey, former British intelligence officer Christopher Steele, the Democratic National Committee and numerous others in a lengthy complaint filed in federal court in Florida. 'Political manifesto' US District Judge Donald Middlebrooks dismissed Trump's lawsuit against Clinton, citing numerous inadequacies, including that Trump had waited too long to bring some of the claims.

items.title: Outrage over plan to livestream US military firing squad execution
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Condemnation of US plans for a public execution by military firing squad escalated on Friday, as Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would be livestreamed as proposed and insisted he would not watch if it was. Nidal Hasan's execution — scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by US military firing squad since 1945. A Pentagon official told AFP on Thursday that the execution would be streamed live, after US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said "we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public".

items.title: Two students murdered, drama at Subang Airport [WATCH]
items.summary: In Yong Peng, 16-year-old student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal was found dead at her school on Oct 3, while in Kuantan, a 19-year-old student, Elisa Jonova Masilamani, was found dead at a house on Oct 6 following an alleged argument with her boyfriend. FORM FOUR STUDENT FOUND DEAD AT JOHOR SCHOOL Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, was found dead at a secondary school in Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, on Oct 3. Police arrested three 16-year-old boys on the same day, with one remanded for six days until Oct 9.

items.title: COURT WATCH: Murder charges, Zara Qairina inquest and major legal challenges [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An e-hailing driver has pleaded not guilty to three charges over a crash that killed a 22-year-old Maldivian student and injured another passenger, including driving under the influence of methamphetamine. The case leads this week's Court Watch, alongside murder charges against two teenagers over the death of their junior, fresh developments in the Zara Qairina inquest, and several significant legal challenges. E-hailing driver charged over crash that killed student, injured another Five days after a crash claimed the life of a 22-year-old Maldivian student, an e-hailing driver was brought before the Shah Alam Magistrate's Court to face three charges linked to the accident, including causing death while driving under the influence of methamphetamine.

items.title: Real inclusion: How Budget 2027 benefits ordinary Malaysians in giving them a share of the country’s wealth and success
items.summary: The national budget totalling RM510 billion, up from RM470 billion in Budget 2026, was tabled amid elevated global fuel prices and Malaysia’s ageing population, and could be the final one before the 16th General Election (GE16). Here’s a snapshot of what makes Budget 2027: Cash assistance and cost of living The government will increase the allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM16 billion, from RM15 billion. STR recipients: All recipients will receive SARA of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 a year, benefiting up to nine million people.

items.title: Set on fire, thrown from cars: Iran’s women stunt performers break barriers
items.summary: TEHRAN, Oct 9 — As evening falls at a Tehran skatepark, a woman calmly steps forward with her body ablaze, performing a daring stunt that challenges convention in front of an impressed Iranian audience. Behind her, young women practise backward flips into a pit filled with foam, following the instructions of Nasrin Teymouri. Iranian coach and stunt woman Nasrin Teymouri (center R) teaches fire techniques to stunt performers Mojgan Nematollahi (C) and Arshia Teymouri (L) during a training session in in Tehran's skatepark, in the capital on September 25, 2026.

items.title: Mexican court finds three men guilty of 2024 killing of Australian, US surfers
items.summary: MEXICO CITY: A Mexican judge on Friday found three men guilty of the 2024 murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend during a surf trip to the state of Baja California, a court source told Reuters. Jesus Gerardo Garcia, known as "El Kekas", and the co-defendants identified simply as Irineo Francisco "N" and Angel Jesus "N", were found guilty of aggravated homicide, violent robbery and vehicle theft by a Baja California court. Their truck was later found burned nearby.

items.title: Boarded windows and evacuations as major hurricane nears US Gulf coast
items.summary: NEW MEXICO: Residents of coastal towns in Florida and Alabama boarded up windows and filled sandbags on Friday as Hurricane Isaias bore down on the US Gulf Coast, bringing life-threatening storm surges and winds of 185 kph. Tens of thousands of people in Florida's Panhandle and along Alabama's Gulf Coast faced mandatory evacuation orders. The Category 3 Isaias, the first hurricane of an unusually quiet season for the United States, was expected to make landfall between Mobile, Alabama, and Grayton Beach in the Florida Panhandle on Friday evening, according to the National Hurricane Centre.

items.title: 7.7-magnitude quake rocks Panama, triggers tsunami warning
items.summary: PENONOME: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake rocked Panama on Friday, causing panic in the high-rise capital and bringing down buildings in the centre of the country, but there were no immediate reports of casualties. In Panama City, about 200km from the epicentre, people rushed to evacuate skyscrapers in scenes of panic. Another showed a bridge over the Panama Canal shaking violently but remaining upright as vehicles travelled across it.

items.title: Sarawak honours five helicopter crash victims posthumously
items.summary: Leading the list was Sabah and Sarawak Chief Judge Datuk Azizah Nawawi, who received the Panglima Negara Bintang Sarawak (PNBS), which carries the title Datuk Seri. Another 22 individuals received the Panglima Setia Bintang Sarawak (PSBS), which carries the title Datuk. Also among the recipients were UiTM Sarawak rector Prof Dr Firdaus Abdullah, Universiti Malaysia Sarawak vice-chancellor Prof Dr Ahmad Hata Rasit, Sarawak Education Department director Omar Mahli and Sarawak Health Department director Dr Veronica Lugah.

items.title: RTD welcomes 2027 Budget road safety measures, including victim compensation
items.summary: Road Transport Department (RTD) director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the amendment was among three key 2027 Budget initiatives welcomed by the Transport Ministry and RTD to strengthen road safety and protect public welfare. He said the ministry and RTD welcomed the mandatory implementation of telematics systems for commercial vehicles to monitor speed, location and risky driving patterns, including the potential integration of alcohol detection devices. Anwar said the government would make telematics systems compulsory for commercial vehicles and that Perkeso would provide health screening vouchers for commercial vehicle drivers.

items.title: Three killed in Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport, including pilot
items.summary: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia said on Friday that three people including a pilot were killed in attacks on Riyadh's international airport the day before, after Yemen's Houthis claimed a series of attacks targeting the facility. The conflict between the Houthis and Yemen's Saudi-backed government has spilled over into the kingdom, with the Iran-backed fighters staging repeated attacks on Saudi targets since launching a lightning offensive just across the border. The Saudi civil aviation authority said two attacks on Thursday on the Saudi capital's airport and a Saudia airlines plane there "resulted in the martyrdom of three citizens."

items.title: ICC hits back at US sanctions, warns 'history will judge this moment'
items.summary: THE HAGUE: The International Criminal Court said Friday that US sanctions on the institution were an attack on international law and warned that "history will judge this moment." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said earlier Friday that Washington would ban transactions with what he called a "rogue court," escalating a long-running campaign by President Donald Trump's administration against the court. The court said such actions were aimed at intimidating ICC staff and disrupting its activities, vowing it would not be deterred.

items.title: Civil servants to get RM1,500 aid, pensioners RM750 under Budget 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 1.3 million civil servants in Grade Utama B and below, including those on contract appointments, will receive RM1,500 in special financial assistance under Budget 2027. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the finance minister, announced the assistance when tabling the Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today. More than one million government pensioners, including pensionable and non-pensionable veterans, will also receive RM750 each.

items.title: Rehda backs Budget 2027 housing measures but calls for more action on rising costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) has welcomed measures in Budget 2027 to support homeownership, while urging the government to do more to address rising development costs and housing affordability. Its president, Datuk Zaini Yusoff, said in a statement that the expanded stamp duty exemptions for first-time homebuyers would help reduce the upfront cost of buying a home. The association also welcomed stamp duty exemptions for rehabilitating abandoned housing projects, saying they could help revive projects and provide relief to affected purchasers.

items.title: PLUS to close Bangi Toll Plaza road shoulder for widening works until June 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — PLUS Malaysia Berhad (PLUS) will temporarily close the road shoulder after the exit lane of the Bangi Toll Plaza towards Bandar Baru Bangi from today until June 28 next year to facilitate road widening works. In a statement today, PLUS said the works were scheduled to take approximately eight months as part of the company’s ongoing efforts to improve highway facilities and enhance users’ comfort. Users are also advised to plan their journeys and obtain the latest traffic updates through the PLUS app, the company’s official social media platforms, including its X account @plustrafik, and electronic message signs (VMS) at selected locations.

items.title: Budget 2027 draws positive response from ministers over focus on living costs, wages and public services
items.summary: Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the measures reflected public feedback gathered through nationwide engagement sessions, particularly concerns over rising living costs and the need for better wages. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, earlier tabled Budget 2027, which places greater emphasis on boosting household disposable income and supporting middle-income earners alongside continued economic reforms. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi speaks during a press conference at Parliament in Kuala Lumpur on October 9, 2026.

items.title: E-Commerce Bill to protect small traders, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government will table an E-Commerce Bill at the next parliamentary sitting to strengthen accountability among online platforms and sellers, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the government was urgently examining legislative and enforcement measures to protect micro, small and medium enterprises from unfair competition and ensure goods purchased by consumers were safe. The fifth Madani Budget, themed “Malaysia Madani: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi”, is the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan.

items.title: Budget 2027: Home, Defence Ministries each allocated RM22b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Home Ministry and Defence Ministry have each been allocated RM22 billion under Budget 2027, tabled in the Dewan Rakyat today. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said RM7.1 billion of the total allocation would be channelled to procure and maintain assets for the armed forces, police, and uniformed agencies under the Home Ministry. Anwar also said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had blocked more than 5.7 billion scam-related calls and SMS messages.

items.title: Malaysia’s approved investments rise 11.7pc to RM218.5b in first half of 2026, says PM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Malaysia’s approved investments rose 11.7 per cent to RM218.5 billion in the first half of 2026, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “For example, Sime Darby Property, the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) have established the RM1.25 billion New Economy Venture Fund to develop data centres and logistics assets in Elmina, Selangor,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today. Meanwhile, he said Khazanah Nasional Bhd and the Retirement Fund (KWAP) had invested RM1.2 billion to help local semiconductor companies move up the value chain.

items.title: Budget 2027: RM2.62b aid for paddy farmers, incentives for fishermen, smallholders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is allocating RM2.62 billion in aid to paddy farmers under Budget 2027, covering various subsidies and incentives to increase rice production and safeguard their welfare. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the assistance would enable paddy farmers to receive benefits of about RM4,300 per hectare of paddy field, including subsidies for seeds, fertiliser, pesticides, ploughing costs and paddy prices. “To rehabilitate and rejuvenate paddy fields, RM20 million will be provided to supply foliar fertiliser for more than 10,000 hectares of paddy fields.

items.title: Budget 2027: RM8b for TVET, 30,000 new job opportunities via BAKAT Madani
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was also targeting 30,000 new job opportunities through the BAKAT Madani initiative next year, including through the participation of private companies. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said that under the overall skills development initiative, HRD Corp, with an allocation of RM3 billion, would offer three million skills training opportunities, including for continuing professional development among professionals. He said the Skills Development Fund Corporation (PTPK) had allocated RM500 million to finance trainees enrolled in skills training programmes at public and private skills training institutes registered with the corporation.

items.title: PM Anwar: Registration to open next week for affordable smart city Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil
items.summary: Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said nearly RM1 billion has also been allocated for projects under the People-Friendly Homes (Rumah Mesra Rakyat) and People's Residency Programme (Program Residensi Rakyat). “Four new housing projects will be implemented in Kulai, Johor; Nilai, Negeri Sembilan; Paya Rumput, Melaka; and Lembah Pertang, Terengganu,” he said. Anwar also announced that the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) will provide housing financing guarantees of up to RM20 billion.

items.title: Budget 2027: Health minister vows to complete 9,000 contract-to-permanent doctor transitions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Health Ministry (MoH) will complete the process of appointing 9,000 contract doctors to permanent positions throughout 2027, effectively ending the interim contract doctor system, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said. When tabling the budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that more than 9,000 contract doctors would be offered permanent positions next year, while doctors who complete their housemanship in the future would be offered permanent posts as medical officers. Anwar also said that since 2023, the Madani Government had appointed more than 15,000 contract doctors to permanent positions, including 4,000 this year.

items.title: Ringgit gains against US dollar as Budget 2027 underscores fiscal discipline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The ringgit closed higher against the US dollar today, supported by the government’s commitment to fiscal consolidation under Budget 2027, an analyst said. At 6pm, the ringgit climbed to 4.0830/0875 against the greenback from yesterday’s close of 4.0890/0940. “The expected narrowing of the fiscal deficit suggests that the government remains committed to fiscal discipline, which can effectively help bolster confidence among traders and investors towards the ringgit,” he told Bernama today.

items.title: ‘Today is for the rakyat, tomorrow is for the wife’: Syed Saddiq’s Budget 2027 reply amuses social media
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Muar Member of Parliament Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman left local social media users amused following his response to a post on Threads. “Today is for the rakyat, tomorrow is for the wife. “From fiancée, to future wife to now just wife, so cute,” commented user nadhrahy_.

items.title: Sabah, with RM18.6b in allocations, hails 2027 budget as alleviating burden for all Malaysians
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 9 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor described the National 2027 Budget as a comprehensive budget that alleviates the people's financial burden and reflects the strength of the country's economy. In Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s proposed budget, Sabah continues to be the biggest recipient of federal allocations with RM18.6 billion for next year, an increase of 6.25 per cent compared to RM17.6 billion for this year. In addition, Anwar said road projects in Sabah and Sarawak would continue with an allocation of RM3.3 billion under the 2027 Budget.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng calls Budget 2027 Anwar’s ‘most reform-minded’ yet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today described Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth Madani Budget as the “most reform-minded” budget yet. Lim, who is also Bagan MP, said expanding the social safety net to gig workers, persons with disabilities and senior citizens, providing more inclusive funding allocations and adjusting personal income tax rates to address past injustices were steps in the right direction. Still, Lim said more needed to be done, particularly by allocating 10 per cent of total Bumiputera allocations to non-Bumiputera communities without reducing existing Bumiputera funding.

items.title: Budget 2027: Medical groups hail end to contract doctor system, enhanced public-private synergy but seek more on retention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Healthcare stakeholders had mixed responses to the national health allocations announced in Budget 2027, with the Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) applauding the move to end the contract doctor system while highlighting critical gaps in workforce retention The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM), meanwhile, welcomed measures to boost public-private cooperation. We commend the Government for taking this important step towards providing greater job security and career certainty for our young doctors,” he said. MMA also said more emphasis should be placed on strengthening primary healthcare to tackle NCDs.

items.title: Four injured after lorry crashes into 11 vehicles in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 9 — Four people were injured in an accident involving a lorry and 11 other vehicles at Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, Alam Budiman here today. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department was informed of the crash at about 4.30pm and immediately dispatched personnel to the scene. “The accident left a man and a woman with serious head injuries, while two other male victims sustained minor injuries,” he said in a statement.

items.title: MEF welcomes RM2,000 minimum wage, says MSME exemption gives smaller firms breathing room
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) today welcomed the federal government’s decision to raise the national minimum wage to RM2,000 while exempting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of less than RM50 million. MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said a balanced approach was essential to ensure efforts to improve workers’ welfare did not inadvertently undermine business viability, discourage hiring or put existing jobs at risk. Explaining further, Syed Hussain said a responsible wage policy focuses not only on the extent of wage increases but also on ensuring businesses can sustain those wages, protect existing jobs and continue creating new employment opportunities.

items.title: Haze: 36 areas record unhealthy API readings, Pasir Gudang highest at 190
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 36 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5.45pm today, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest reading at 190. In Negeri Sembilan, three areas recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Seremban (189), Nilai (183) and Port Dickson (174), while in Melaka, the affected areas were Bukit Rambai (187), Bandaraya Melaka (183) and Alor Gajah (181). A total of 32 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while no areas recorded good readings.

items.title: Budget 2027: Government-owned Entities Bill to be drafted next year, RM1.1b for enforcement agencies’ operations
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Finance Minister, made the announcement while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today. “With the Government Procurement Act coming to force starting 2027, the government will improve transparency and publish project details, including the contractors and contract value,” Anwar said. Anwar also said revenue generated from loan repayments, including from education and business loans, disbursed to federal statutory bodies must only be used for the approved purposes and target groups.

items.title: Budget 2027: Bumiputera contractor procurement nearly doubles to RM7.5b, GLICs to invest RM2b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is set to increase the procurement allocation for Bumiputera contractors in the G1 to G4 grades to RM7.5 billion under Budget 2027, an increase from RM4 billion this year. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this follows recent concerns raised by Bumiputera contractors and companies. “This also provides opportunities for Bumiputera construction, engineering, and maintenance companies.
